trustedEnforcementDesign: GitHub `pull_request` runs are read-only (contents: read, persist-credentials: false). The workflow verifies checkout/event integrity, then checks out the PROTECTED BASE commit into ../trusted-base and executes the boundary validator FROM THE BASE against the head diff (name-status) plus trusted event metadata. The PR head is treated as data; a head that weakens the validator/lineage/roles/workflow cannot change the enforcement root used for its own run. Enforcement-root changes are permitted only for an implementation/correction-role governed record and are therefore gated by the prior trusted policy. No untrusted head code is executed under privileged context.
taskCapabilityModel: roles.mjs: implementation/correction => modify enumerated implementation paths + exactly 2 result files; validation/closeout => exactly their 2 result records only; setup (*_CONTRACT.md/*_STATE.json/*_PROMPT.md/CLAUDE_*.md) immutable; no whole-directory prefix authorization.
ancestryGovernanceModel: govrecord.mjs: owner *_STATE.json record binds taskId/role(from branch)/head/base/approvedBaseSha; boundary requires the record + head-descends-approvedBase; lineage.mjs no longer preauthorizes any task by branch name.

acceptedV11BacklogLimitations.D: Broader current-record lifecycle refinements beyond exact role inventory; the exact two-result-file + immutable-setup rule is enforced, deeper lifecycle states are backlog.
acceptedV11BacklogLimitations.H: Marker-protocol enum compatibility extensions (e.g. additional governed outcome enums); the controlled enum set is enforced and can be extended without a security change.
acceptedV11BacklogLimitations.K: Richer history event/timestamp semantics (ISO event schema); current history integrity + append-only is enforced, richer semantics are backlog.

ciRemediationR1.failedStep: Discover changed files and trusted event metadata (fail-closed)
ciRemediationR1.exactFailure: actions/checkout@v4 on the pull_request event checked out GitHub's synthetic merge commit a80bb7c ('Merge 6b8c771 into 07d0e38'), so `git rev-parse HEAD` (a80bb7c) != trusted event head SHA 6b8c771. The V4-C7 guard `[ git rev-parse HEAD = HEAD_SHA ]` correctly failed the step ('checked-out HEAD != trusted head sha', exit 1); trusted-base and boundary steps were skipped. The integrity check worked as designed; the workflow's own checkout used the wrong ref.

fixes.checkoutHeadSha: The workflow now checks out `ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha` so HEAD == the trusted head SHA; the V4-C7 integrity guard is retained unchanged and still fails closed on any real mismatch.
fixes.trustedBaseBootstrap: The approved base 07d0e38 predates the V4 policy modules, so running the base validator with V4 flags is impossible for the transition PR. lib/bootstrap.mjs adds a pinned one-time BOOTSTRAP anchor (immutable approvedBaseSha 07d0e38 + frozenSetupSha 063078a, bound to Issue #60/PR #61/exact head+base branches). resolveEnforcement returns DESCENDANT when the approved base carries V4 policy (every normal PR and Final Acceptance 017 -> run from the protected base), BOOTSTRAP only for this exact anchored range, and REJECT otherwise. The old base is never run with unsupported V4 flags, and mutable PR-head policy is never silently used as trusted enforcement for a non-anchored range.
fixes.frozenSetupBoundary: The owner setup phase (approvedBase 07d0e38 -> frozenSetup 063078a) is verified to introduce EXACTLY the three governed setup files (additions only) via `check-setup-phase`. The worker boundary is evaluated from the frozen setup SHA -> head, the governed record is read from the frozen setup tree (the head cannot rewrite its own governing record), setup files are immutable afterward, and no arbitrary third setup/result file is allowed.

ciRemediationR2.descendantSetupPathDefect: The R1 DESCENDANT path ran the boundary with base-sha = the protected base and diff = base..head. For a real NEW governed task the owner setup STATE record does not exist at the protected base (it is added on the new branch), so govRecordAt(protectedBase) returned null and the boundary failed 'no owner-created governed record'; and the new branch's setup-file ADDITIONS appeared in the diff and were rejected as immutable setup files. A real new validation/correction task could therefore never bootstrap under DESCENDANT.
ciRemediationR2.design: A generic frozen owner-setup boundary is now discovered from the protected-base policy. lib/bootstrap.mjs adds classifyCanonicalSetupBase / isCanonicalSetupPath / checkDescendantSetupPhase / discoverFrozenSetupBoundary. The CLI `discover-setup-boundary` derives the task result dir from the full approvedBase..head diff, walks the ordered commits (git rev-list --reverse + git diff-tree -z per commit), and locates the UNIQUE frozen owner-setup boundary: the last commit of the maximal initial run of setup-only commits. It requires the setup phase to add exactly the role-specific canonical triple (one *_CONTRACT.md, one *_STATE.json, one CLAUDE_*_PROMPT.md) under the result dir, additions only; rejects implementation/result files before the boundary, missing/duplicate/ambiguous/multiple boundaries, and setup mutation after the freeze. The workflow DESCENDANT branch now: executes policy from the protected base (../trusted-base), discovers the frozen setup boundary, reads the governed *_STATE.json from the frozen setup commit (base-sha = frozen setup for the boundary CLI), binds the approved base for ancestry, and evaluates the worker diff ONLY frozen-setup -> trusted head. Governance authority is never read from mutable worker-head content.
ciRemediationR2.genericSetupInventoryRule: Derived from task role + result directory + canonical setup naming: exactly one <PREFIX>_CONTRACT.md, one <PREFIX>_STATE.json and one CLAUDE_<PREFIX>_PROMPT.md directly under the result directory (validation role: exactly the contract, state and Claude prompt setup records).
ciRemediationR2.bootstrapAnchorUnchanged: The one-time V4 BOOTSTRAP anchor remains pinned to Issue #60 / PR #61 only; it was NOT broadened, and Final Acceptance 017 / any future branch is NOT preauthorized.

remainingLimitations: The trusted-base enforcement and merge/ancestry/checkout facts are enforced in CI where Git and the base checkout are available; GitHub Actions cannot be executed locally, so those runtime steps are correct-by-construction and the deterministic policy cores are library-verified (177/0).

For a stacked PR the owner setup commits and executor work commits share the branch; the governed record is validated as identity-bound data with setup-file immutability and ancestry, rather than by per-commit authorship separation.
D/H/K remain accepted V1.1 backlog limitations and are not V5 triggers.
